latest_rss.title: Crossing Snowcapped Mountains
latest_rss.summary: In June 1935, the Central Red Army arrived at the foot of Mount Jiajin and began to cross the first major snow-capped mountain on the Long March. The main peak rises to 4,930 meters and is snow-clad year-round, with thin, rarefied air. A local folk song says, "Mount Jiajin, Mount Jiajin – even birds cannot fly over it, and no ordinary mortal can scale it." The Red Army troops, poorly clad against the cold and short of food, pushed forward through wind, snow, and hail, relying on chili water for warmth and wooden sticks for support. From June 12 to 18, over the course of seven days and nights, the entire main force successfully crossed Mount Jiajin.

latest_rss.title: Book fairs, shows and forums highlight Xinjiang Reading Conference
latest_rss.summary: The third Xinjiang National Reading Conference has kicked off in Hotan, Xinjiang under the theme of "Deepening Nationwide Reading." The event aims to foster a love for books and strengthen cultural identity. At the opening ceremony, model campuses, families and enterprises were honored, 10 reading promoters appointed, and 35 recommended Xinjiang books published in 2025 were released. The conference also featured book fairs, an evening reading performance and forums on youth reading. Parallel activities were held across Hotan to encourage people to make reading part of daily life.
